core.title: Read every provided appendix before planning from it
core.given: The user's input includes an appendix (file path, file URL, or 'appendix:' mention).
core.when: You are about to create a planning output (one of the stack's plan artifact kinds, profile: roles.plan_artifact.kinds) or to ask what the user wants to create.
core.then: Read the appendix with the designated file-reading tool (profile: idiom.file_read_tool) and grasp what it shows (multi-screen flow, single component, architecture, etc.) before producing the output or the question.
prefer: Read an appendix in a format the designated file-reading tool consumes directly as multimodal input (exactly the formats listed in profile: tooling.appendix_readable_formats) as multimodal input rather than treating it as an opaque attachment.

Analyze by type: mockup → UI components, layouts, flows, states, interactions, responsive variants; spreadsheet → business rules, calculations, data models, validation constraints; document → requirements, constraints, specifications, acceptance criteria; diagram → architecture, entities, sequences, state transitions, relationships; audio → transcribe, extract user pain points, requirements, context, clarifications; video → workflows, interactions, pain points, existing behavior patterns.

When creating, enrich the output with the appendix's type-specific content appropriate to that output's kind: apply the entries of the kind-keyed enrichment map for the kind being created (the concrete map is realization data; the kinds come from the profile's plan artifact kinds) — e.g. more accurate description and a domain model from diagrams/documents; behavioral step statements from flows/interactions; an acceptance harness matched to the appendix type (mockup → visual, diagram → integration); component clustering from mockup sections; component props/state/behavior from mockups and diagrams — not the entire list for every output.
Grounded question shape: state what the appendix shows (e.g. 'I see your mockup shows a login form'), then ask what the user wants to create.
avoid: Planning from the text request alone, ignoring a provided appendix.
When creating: producing an output not enriched with the appendix's type-specific content appropriate to that output's kind (prefer[1], prefer[2]). Required.
When creating: leaving the appendix unreferenced in the output's manifest. Required step; manifest structure is defined by the artifact schema, not this convention.

When intent is unclear (the request names no plannable artifact kind): asking an abstract question that ignores the appendix, e.g. 'What do you want to build?'. The question must cite what the appendix shows.
core.why: Appendices only reduce ambiguity if consumed — to enrich generated artifacts and to ground routing questions in concrete content, cutting confusion and back-and-forth.
evidence: The planner transcript shows the appendix was read (a call of the designated file-reading tool, profile: idiom.file_read_tool, on the referenced path/URL) before the output or question was produced.

Created artifacts contain details traceable to the appendix's type-specific content (e.g. components/flows from a mockup, entities from a diagram, rules from a spreadsheet), and acceptance harnesses match the appendix type (mockup → visual, diagram → integration).
When an output was created, its manifest references the appendix (in the schema-defined manifest structure).
Clarification questions asked after an appendix was provided without clear intent name concrete content from it (e.g. screens, entities, components) rather than being abstract.
verification: No automated detector exists for this rule (implementation type none); compliance is judged by an LLM or reviewer from the planner transcript and the created artifacts.
Appendix detection is pattern-based: a file path in the user input, the literal 'appendix:', or a file URL.

Disambiguation flow to check: the planner reads the appendix with the designated file-reading tool, grasps what it shows (multi-screen flow, single component, architecture, etc.), then asks a clarification question grounded in that content; both an open follow-up and an options list are acceptable — what matters is the grounding statement.

Creation workflow order to check: detect → read multimodally (the directly consumable formats per the profile) → analyze by type → enrich the output with the kind-appropriate type-specific content → reference the appendix in the manifest; the manifest structure itself is defined by the artifact schema, not by this convention.

fires: User asks the planner to create a planning output (one of the stack's plan artifact kinds) and attaches a mockup, diagram, spreadsheet, document, audio or video file.
User message contains 'appendix:' followed by a file path or URL.
User provides an appendix without an intent keyword naming a plannable artifact kind, so the planner must ask a clarifying question.
doesNotFire: Planner request with no file path, file URL or 'appendix:' mention.
Coder or tester work that does not author planner artifacts.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete kinds of planning output the planner can author; the core says 'planning output' / 'plannable artifact kind' and this key supplies the stack's enumeration (used by when, the kind-conditioned enrichment guidance and the unclear-intent condition).

The tool the agent must use to read a referenced file path or URL; it restores the concrete named-tool read requirement of then, evidence[0] and the verification flow, so the instantiated core requires exactly the realization's read tool rather than any file-read operation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the Read tool — the planner reads the referenced appendix path/URL by invoking the Read tool, and the compliance evidence is a Read tool call in the transcript

profileRequirements.meaning: The appendix formats the stack's reading tool consumes directly as multimodal input; core.prefer[0] applies exactly to these formats and to no others, so the instantiated preference covers exactly the realization's enumerated formats.
profileRequirements.bunValue: PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF, audio, video (read directly as multimodal input)

profileRequirements.meaning: How a referenced appendix's concrete observable format/kind is classified into an analysis type, selecting the type-specific analysis; supplies the observer's concrete observable values for the activation file_kind fact, whose core values are the neutral analysis types.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Observable kinds: png, jpg, svg, pdf, audio, video, spreadsheet, document, diagram; the observer classifies the referenced appendix by type (mockup, spreadsheet, document, diagram, audio, video) to select the type-specific analysis

proposedKeys.meaning: The tool the agent uses to read a referenced file path or URL (multimodal where applicable); transcript calls of this tool are the compliance evidence for read-before-use rules.
proposedKeys.bunValue: the Read tool — the planner reads the referenced appendix path/URL by invoking the Read tool, and the compliance evidence is a Read tool call in the transcript
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group binds boundary, validation and machinery constructs and the tooling group binds build/test commands, but no existing key names the agent's file-reading tool, which this appendix rule needs so its core can require the realization's named reader rather than any file-read operation.

proposedKeys.meaning: The appendix formats the stack's agent tooling (its designated file-reading tool) consumes directly as multimodal input; read-before-plan rules scope their multimodal-reading preference exactly to this list.
proposedKeys.bunValue: PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF, audio, video (read directly as multimodal input)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The suffix group classifies repository source, test, markup and plan files by name suffix, and the tooling group covers package manager, languages, test runner and URN resolver; no existing key describes which appendix formats the stack's reading tool consumes directly as multimodal input.

proposedKeys.meaning: How a referenced appendix's concrete observable format/kind is classified into an analysis type (e.g. mockup, spreadsheet, document, diagram, audio, video) to select type-specific analysis; supplies the observer values for appendix-type activation facts.
proposedKeys.bunValue: Observable kinds: png, jpg, svg, pdf, audio, video, spreadsheet, document, diagram; the observer classifies the referenced appendix by type (mockup, spreadsheet, document, diagram, audio, video) to select the type-specific analysis
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No existing key describes how a user-provided appendix's concrete format is classified into an analysis type; the suffix keys classify repository source files, not user-provided appendices, and no idiom or tooling key covers this capability mapping.

bunOnly.text: Enrichment map when creating: wagon → more accurate description, domain model from diagrams/docs; WMBT → better when/must/then from flows/interactions; acceptance → harness (mockup→visual, diagram→integration); feature → component clustering from mockup sections; component → props/state/behavior from mockups and diagrams.
bunOnly.reason: The enrichment map is keyed by the stack's concrete plan artifact kinds and assigns different enrichments to different kinds; the core keeps only the kind-conditioned obligation (apply the entries for the kind being created) and each stack supplies its own keyed map.

neutralityNotes: This is an agent-behavior rule, so most content is already stack-neutral. Points: (1) The concrete plan-artifact kinds (wagon, WMBT, acceptance, feature, component) are stack-local and enter the core only through the profile key roles.plan_artifact.kinds; the intent keywords in avoid[3] and the phase-fact note are those same names and survive concretely only in the realization. (2) The Bun read requirement names a concrete tool ('Read the appendix with the Read tool', evidence 'Read tool call in the transcript'); the core says 'the designated file-reading tool' and binds it via the proposed key idiom.file_read_tool (Bun value: the Read tool), so instantiation imposes exactly Bun's named-tool obligation. (3) The directly multimodal-readable formats are capability data bound via the proposed key tooling.appendix_readable_formats (Bun value: PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF, audio, video); core.prefer[0] applies exactly to that list, so it is neither broader nor narrower than the realization's enumeration, and the core names no concrete formats. (4) The appendix-type observer's concrete observable kinds (png, jpg, svg, pdf, audio, video, spreadsheet, document, diagram) and its format-to-type classification are capability data bound via the proposed key tooling.appendix_type_map; the core activation fact keeps only the neutral analysis types (mockup, spreadsheet, document, diagram, audio, video). (5) The enrichment obligation is kind-conditioned in the core (apply the entries of the kind-keyed map for the kind being created, not the entire list); the concrete wagon/WMBT/acceptance/feature/component map is bunOnly realization data. (6) The output 'manifest' is kept as a neutral artifact concept because the rule itself defers its structure to the artifact schema.
